evidence.reason: The finding is a genuine durability gap in existing intended behavior, not a scope enlargement. claim_run_dir creates the record base and the run directory (lines 606-612) without fsyncing the parent directory that records the new run-dir entry. The recovery receipt itself is written via durable_write, whose fsync-based persistence shows power-loss durability is intended; but fsyncing the receipt's own directory cannot persist the run_dir entry that lives in the record base. So after a crash, the base can be missing the run directory (and thus the prior SHA/trigger evidence) even while the run was admitted/host held, which is exactly the kind of crash-safety inconsistency durable_write exists to prevent. The fix the finding asks for is small and compatible: fsync the record base after mkdir of run_dir, fsync the new base's parent when parents=True created it, and fail closed on either. This is an ordinary correctness repair of the durability the code already attempts, so it does not require owner judgment.
